issues.body: In `_apt_packages_in_line`, the command-position arm `[[ $cmd_pos -eq 1 && "$tok" == ?*=* ]] && continue` classifies the raw token as an assignment without checking whether the assignment word is quoted. For example, `RUN "FOO=bar" apt-get install -y jq python3-yaml` does not execute apt-get: the shell treats the quoted first word as the command name `FOO=bar` and fails. The parser sees an even quote count, then accepts that token as an assignment prefix, leaves `cmd_pos=1`, and reports both packages. `_assert_container_selftest_deps` consequently returns success for an image that installs neither dependency. This is a fail-open trust-check result.
issues.fix_hint: Recognize assignment prefixes according to shell quoting semantics, declining to count packages whenever that classification is uncertain. Add a regression fixture through `_assert_container_selftest_deps` using a quoted assignment-shaped command word and expect `missing`, plus retain an unquoted `FOO=bar apt-get ...` positive control expecting `satisfied`.
issues.title: Quoted assignment-shaped command words can fabricate installed packages

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

Round 4 introduces a new fail-open lexical case in the Dockerfile dependency checker. The assignment-prefix recognition operates on the raw token and therefore treats a quoted assignment-shaped command word as an environment assignment. That can make the gate accept packages from an apt-get command the shell never reaches. Because round 3 had no findings and approved, progress is regressing.
